capitals.name: Amanvi
capitals.note: The Gyaman page says royal authority was 'centered at Amanvi'; it gives no coordinates. The Bondoukou point (8°2′N 2°48′W on the Bondoukou page) is used, as the page ties the Abron kingdom's hub to Bondoukou.

correction.text: the Gyaman kingdom round Bondoukou and Sampa: Banda, Jaman and Bonduku, from the Black Volta to the Comoe basin

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The Gyaman page gives no area and no frontier, only the towns (Amanvi, Sampa, Bondoukou, Kong, Begho) and the regions Banda, Jaman and Bonduku and the Black Volta; an 80 km circle round Bondoukou (about 20,000 km2) is a stand-in. The 1897 partition between France and Britain follows the modern Ivory Coast/Ghana border in this reading.

ledger.note: 17th century: the infobox period is '17th century'; Aduana clan migrants left Akwamu after succession disputes and settled near Suntreso and Asantemanso; the date of Gyaman's formation is not on the page. Bondoukou page: conquered by the Abron in the 'early seventeenth century' and 'soon became the economic hub of the Gyaaman kingdom'. Entered at the start of the century.

1740-1741: 'Asante forces defeated Gyaman and destroyed its capital, reducing it to tributary status'; regular tribute to Asante from c. 1740. The Ashanti dossier (af-04-a) dates the Gyaman invasion 1732.
c. 1817: Kwadwo Adinkra 'stopped paying tribute and declared independence' (he came to power c. 1800).
1818: Asante invasion; 'Adinkra was killed (accounts differ on how)'. Page gives no month and no battle sites.
1819: 'Asante made Gyaman a province, imposed military occupation, and barred direct coastal trade'.
1819: Gyaman becomes an Asante province under military occupation.

1874: 'after the British invasion of Kumasi, Gyaman regained political autonomy' (no specific end date on the page; the same page has tribute to Asante c. 1740-1875). The Ashanti dossier has Gyaman as a vassal to 1895.
13 November 1888: the French officer Treich-Laplene signed a 'Protectorate treaty' with the Abron king of Bondoukou (Gyaman page: 'Gyamanhene signed a treaty of protection with France').
1895: 'Samori Toure attacked Gyaman'. Bondoukou page: the city 'fell to Samori between September 1895 and July 1897' and he 'deposed the Abron in favour of the Muslim Dyula'.
1897: the French protectorate over Gyaman ends in the partition; Bondoukou page: 'the French incorporated the town into French West Africa in 1899'.

notes: Gyaman has no Cliopatria row. Two pages. Dates conflict with other dossiers: the Ashanti dossier (af-04-a) has the Asante invasion in 1732 and Gyaman a vassal until 1895; the Gyaman page has the defeat in 1740-41, independence about 1817, reconquest 1818-19, Asante occupation until 1874 and tribute 'c. 1740-1875'; the page's own account is not fully consistent (tribute to 1875 against independence about 1817). The founding is only '17th century' and the 1600 start is a bridge. The 1897 split follows the modern Ivory Coast/Ghana border through an 80 km circle at Bondoukou; the page names no frontier. French counterparts use the Cliopatria aggregate slug french-africa; a French West Africa / Ivory Coast colony dossier (af-08) would be the better counterpart. Gazetteer: Sampa is not a place name in it (not used).
